LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is a standard AppImage packaging script for a Discord alternative application. The source is downloaded from the project's own official installer domain (`installer.rootapp.com`) and is verified with a proper SHA256 checksum (not `SKIP`), which is good security practice. The `prepare()` function makes the AppImage executable and extracts it via the standard `--appimage-extract` mechanism, and `package()` installs the extracted contents to `/opt/rootapp-bin/`, creates a `/usr/bin/rootapp` symlink, and installs the desktop entry and icon. Dependencies (`gtk3`, `nss`, `libnotify`, `alsa-lib`, `xdg-utils`, `at-spi2-core`, `fuse2`) are all typical for an Electron-based desktop application, and the `x-scheme-handler/rootapp` MIME type registration is a common pattern for chat apps to handle authentication callbacks. There are no suspicious network requests, no obfuscated commands, no use of `eval`/`base64`/`curl|bash`, no data exfiltration, and no deviations from standard packaging practices.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard AppImage packaging with proper checksum and no malicious behavior.</summary>
</security_assessment>
